verdict.line: You win by keeping Mini Gnar at range and punishing Sett's cooldowns; you lose when you transform into Mega Gnar in his face and eat his E-into-stun combo.

brief.thesis: Sett has zero gap-closers besides his 490-range E (Facebreaker) and 400-range R (Show Stopper), while Mini Gnar's 1100-range Q and Hyper (W) move speed let you dictate distance for free. The whole matchup flips on your Rage bar: the moment it fills and you transform into Mega Gnar, you trade your kiting kit for a melee stun-and-slam right next to a champion whose Q and E are built to punish exactly that lack of distance. It's an even head-to-head (51.9% over 2143 games) with Sett holding the solo-kill edge, so the result comes down to who controls the transform and trade sequencing, not raw stats.

theirWindow.when: You transform into Mega Gnar mid-trade
theirWindow.what: Mega Gnar loses W's Hyper move speed and E's bounce, leaving you planted in front of Sett. That's when his Q (Knuckle Down, two bonus-damage autos scaling off your max health) and E (Facebreaker, 490 range, pulls enemies on opposite sides together for a stun) chain into real damage you can't walk away from.

yourWindow.what: Poke freely with Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown, slows on hit, catching it cuts the cooldown) from outside his auto and E range, then walk back using W's Hyper move speed bonus. Sett has no dash, so this is a clean, repeatable kite window.

start.why: 51.7% win rate over 1808 games and the most-picked start (67.7%); the extra health and sustain let Mini Gnar keep trading Q pokes through Sett's passive Pit Grit regen without losing the war of attrition.

boots.why: 52% win rate over 2193 games (84.3% pick); Sett's damage is almost entirely through his alternating left/right punch autos and Q's two empowered autos, so flat reduction on basic attacks directly cuts his main damage source.

runes.keystoneWhy: 50.2% win rate at 36.3% pick, the top-performing page; the heal and move speed proc directly support the poke-and-retreat pattern you need against a melee champion with no dash.

summoners.why: 51.9% win rate at 70.4% pick, the clear preferred setup; Teleport lets you reset after a poke-heavy trade and get back before Sett can punish a cooldown gap or snowball the lane alone.

playing.title: Track your Rage bar constantly
playing.detail: Don't let yourself transform into Mega Gnar while standing in Sett's face. Bait the transform by backing off or walking into your own wave first, so you don't lose your kiting kit at the worst moment.

playing.title: Poke at max Q range
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100; Sett's autos and his 490-range E don't. Stay outside both, land Q, and catch the return throw to cut the cooldown further.

playing.title: Don't Hop next to his wave
playing.detail: Sett's E (Facebreaker) pulls enemies on opposite sides of him together for a stun, but only slows if you're alone on one side. Land E (Hop/Crunch) beside him, not between him and a minion, or he catches both ends.

playing.title: Watch for an un-cast Haymaker
playing.detail: Sett's W stores all damage he takes as Grit and converts it to a shield plus a true-damage-center punch on cast. If he's been tanking your poke without using it, expect a big burst the moment he does.

playing.title: All-in right after his E or R
playing.detail: Facebreaker (16-10s cd) and Show Stopper (120-80s cd) are his only lockdown tools. The moment either goes on cooldown without landing a kill, Mini Gnar can trade in free of a stun.

playing.title: Choose your transform moment
playing.detail: If you're about to pop into Mega Gnar anyway, try to do it while already on top of Sett (right after landing E) so you get the W stun instead of losing your kite mid-retreat.

playing.title: Itemize into his autos
playing.detail: Plated Steelcaps and Black Cleaver both cut into Sett's alternating punch passive and his Q's empowered autos, which make up the bulk of his sustained damage.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are pulled from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning about Rage timing, the E-into-stun interaction, and the trade windows is my own tactical read, not measured data.
